Huang, Meng and Yang (2009) DBH–height models for Alberta black spruce

Source: R/hd_huang2009.R
hd_huang2009.Rd

Vectorized implementation of the population-level Chapman–Richards height–diameter models of Huang, Meng and Yang (2009) for black spruce (PICE.MAR) in Alberta. Predicts total tree height (m) from DBH (cm) alone (base model 9), or from DBH and top height (model 10), or from DBH, top height and stand basal area (model 11).

Usage

hd_huang2009(DBH, species, HTOP = NULL, BA = NULL, keep_model_id = FALSE)

Arguments

DBH

Numeric vector. Tree level. Diameter at breast height (1.3 m above ground), in cm. Must be >= 0.

species

Character vector. Tree level. NFI species code; only "PICE.MAR" is supported (compact "PICEMAR" is accepted).

HTOP

Optional numeric vector. Plot level. Top height (m): "the average height of the 100 largest DBH trees per ha" (source "TopH", p. 5). This is not the mean height of dominant and codominant trees (HDOM). Must be > 0. Supply to use model 10, or with BA for model 11.

BA

Optional numeric vector. Plot level. Stand basal area per ha (m²/ha) (source "BA", p. 5). The source does not state a minimum DBH or species basis for this total. Must be > 0. Requires HTOP.

keep_model_id

Logical. If TRUE, add column model_id ("huang2009_m9", "huang2009_m10" or "huang2009_m11").

Value

A tibble with column height (m) and, if keep_model_id = TRUE, model_id.

Details

Model scope: black spruce only. Fitted to 93 Alberta permanent sample plots (917 trees) in the Lower Foothills natural region and validated on 71 plots in the Boreal Mixedwood and Upper Foothills (p. 4).

Model forms (eqs. 9–11, pp. 4–5): $$(9): H = 1.3 + \beta_1 [1 - \exp(-\beta_2 DBH)]^{\beta_3};$$ $$(10): H = 1.3 + (\beta_1 + \beta_4 HTOP) [1 - \exp(-\beta_2 DBH)]^{\beta_3};$$ $$(11): H = 1.3 + (\beta_1 + \beta_4 HTOP + \beta_5 BA) [1 - \exp(-\beta_2 DBH)]^{\beta_3}.$$

Height convention: total tree height; DBH measured at 1.3 m, so predicted height tends to 1.3 m as DBH tends to 0.

Population-level prediction: coefficients are the fixed effects of the nonlinear mixed models (Table 2, p. 13), evaluated with the plot random effects on \(\beta_1\) and \(\beta_3\) set to zero (the source's "fixed only" predictions, Table 3). Plot-specific calibration with measured heights is not implemented. The authors report that fixed-only predictions are biased for individual plots and on average (Table 4: mean bias −7.5%, −2.1% and −3.3% of mean height on the validation data for models 9, 10 and 11), and that the base model (9) gave the most accurate calibrated predictions despite ranking last by AIC/BIC. The ratio correction they describe (eqs. 29–30) has no published value and is not applied.

Variants: if HTOP and BA are NULL (default), model 9 is used; if only HTOP is supplied, model 10; if both are supplied, model 11. Supplying BA without HTOP is an error. A one-time message reports the variant used.

Rows with NA in any input return NA height. Inputs outside the range of the fitting data (Table 1: DBH and, where used, HTOP and BA) are computed and reported in a single warning.

References

Huang, S., Meng, S. X., and Yang, Y. (2009). Using nonlinear mixed model technique to determine the optimal tree height prediction model for black spruce. Modern Applied Science, 3(4), 3–18. doi:10.5539/mas.v3n4p3

See also

hd_model_registry(), get_hd_model_info(), hd_huang2016()

Examples

# Model 9: DBH only
hd_huang2009(DBH = c(7.9, 10.7, 20.3), species = "PICE.MAR")
#> hd_huang2009(): using model 9 (DBH only).
#> This message is displayed once per session.
#> # A tibble: 3 × 1
#>   height
#>    <dbl>
#> 1   8.58
#> 2  10.7 
#> 3  16.5 

# Model 10: with top height
hd_huang2009(DBH = c(7.9, 10.7, 20.3), species = "PICE.MAR", HTOP = 14.5)
#> hd_huang2009(): using model 10 (DBH and top height `HTOP`).
#> This message is displayed once per session.
#> # A tibble: 3 × 1
#>   height
#>    <dbl>
#> 1   8.50
#> 2  10.6 
#> 3  15.5 

# Model 11: with top height and basal area
hd_huang2009(
  DBH = c(7.9, 10.7, 20.3), species = "PICE.MAR",
  HTOP = 14.5, BA = 7.75, keep_model_id = TRUE
)
#> hd_huang2009(): using model 11 (DBH, top height `HTOP` and basal area `BA`).
#> This message is displayed once per session.
#> # A tibble: 3 × 2
#>   height model_id     
#>    <dbl> <chr>        
#> 1   8.45 huang2009_m11
#> 2  10.5  huang2009_m11
#> 3  15.2  huang2009_m11

# Inside dplyr::mutate() with tree and plot data
trees <- data.frame(
  DBH = c(8, 15, 22),
  species = "PICE.MAR",
  HTOP = c(14, 14, 19), BA = c(10, 10, 25)
)
dplyr::mutate(trees, hd_huang2009(DBH, species, HTOP, BA))
#>   DBH  species HTOP BA    height
#> 1   8 PICE.MAR   14 10  8.433155
#> 2  15 PICE.MAR   14 10 12.822909
#> 3  22 PICE.MAR   19 25 18.575681
